intro: The taxable turnover thresholds at which a business must register for VAT or may apply to cancel its registration, and the difference between exempt supplies and zero-rated ones.
explanation:
## VAT applies to taxable supplies, not exempt ones

**Value Added Tax (VAT)** applies to taxable supplies, which include standard-rated, reduced-rated and zero-rated goods and services. Some supplies carry no VAT at all. Exempt supplies, such as financial services and many property transactions, are not taxable and do not count towards taxable turnover, and exempt is not the same as zero-rated. Others, such as donations to charities, fall outside the scope of VAT altogether.

## Registration thresholds differ by business type and location

A business established in the UK must register in either of two cases: its taxable turnover over the past 12 months has passed {fact:vat_registration_threshold}, or it expects turnover to pass that amount within the next 30 days. Businesses not established in the UK — known as non-established taxable persons (NETPs) — face a different rule: they must register from the very first taxable sale they make in the UK, with no threshold applying.

Going over the threshold for only a short time can be handled by asking HMRC for a registration exception. A business whose taxable supplies are mainly zero-rated can ask HMRC to be exempt from registering, but a non-established business qualifies only if all of its taxable supplies are zero-rated.

Northern Ireland has two registration thresholds that apply nowhere else in the UK. One is a distance selling threshold, counted over a calendar year's sales. The other covers relevant acquisitions, and since 2021 these have only been possible into Northern Ireland.

## Cancelling a VAT registration and putting things right

Once registered, a business can apply to cancel its VAT registration if its taxable turnover falls below {fact:vat_deregistration_threshold}. Cancellation cannot be backdated: a fall in turnover does not let a business cancel for a period that has already passed.

A NETP cannot use the turnover limit to cancel. It can cancel only once it has made its last taxable supply in the UK.

A business unhappy with how HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) dealt with a registration or deregistration can raise it first with the person or office it has been dealing with, and make a formal complaint if that does not settle it.
